title: Target stand structures by habitat class for the Knife Creek Mule Deer Winter Range
source_document: Alex Fraser Research Forest Management and Working Plan #3 (January 1, 2007)
figure_caption: Target stand structures by habitat class for the Knife Creek Mule Deer Winter Range, comparing density (stems/ha on left, basal area on right axis) by diameter class.

extraction.review_note: Overlay checked; lines and bar tops follow the plotted series. Legend swatches were masked before extraction. Zero values beyond each habitat class maximum DBH are recorded explicitly.

caveats: Figure 11 is a target diagram, not observed plot data.

The recovered per-class basal areas sum to about 17.02, 22.96 and 30.17 m2/ha for Low, Moderate and High, versus Table 29 targets of 16, 22 and 29 m2/ha. Do not force the figure to close; use Table 29 as the policy target and Figure 11 as the relative diameter-distribution shape.
The recovered density distribution implies q-factors of 1.306, 1.254 and 1.253 for Low, Moderate and High, versus Table 29 values of 1.30, 1.25 and 1.25. This is a shape check, not a recalibration.
The figure has no uncertainty bands; recovered values are approximate to the plotted line and bar resolution.
The map on MWP #3 page 162 is schematic and was not used to georeference this table.
